title: Grilled Steaks with Hollandaise Sauce
description: Premium grilled beef steaks cooked to your preferred doneness and served with a classic French Hollandaise sauce. Finished with elegant garnishes for a true Continental fine-dining experience.

ingredients.title: For the Steaks
items: Premium beef tenderloin or ribeye steaks – 2 (200–250 g each, 1½ inches thick)

ingredients.title: For the Hollandaise Sauce
items: White wine vinegar – 2 tbsp (or lemon juice for a milder flavor)
Unsalted butter, clarified and warm – 150 g (10 tbsp)
Dijon mustard – ½ tsp (optional, for stability and depth)
Cayenne or white pepper – a pinch
Lemon juice – a few drops (to finish)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Steaks
steps: Bring steaks to room temperature (about 30 minutes before cooking).
Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels — moisture prevents a good sear.
Brush both sides with olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Grill the Steaks
steps: Use a heavy cast-iron grill pan or outdoor grill preheated to high heat.
Lightly oil the grill grates or pan.
Place steaks on the grill — do not move them for the first 2–3 minutes to ensure perfect grill marks.
Turn 90° for crosshatch marks, then flip after 4–5 minutes (depending on thickness).
Baste lightly with clarified butter infused with rosemary and garlic.
Cook to desired doneness: Rare – 50°C / 122°F, Medium-rare – 55°C / 131°F, Medium – 60°C / 140°F.
Rest steaks for 5–8 minutes, tented with foil. This allows juices to redistribute.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Make the Hollandaise
steps: Technique: Bain-Marie (Double Boiler Method).
In a heatproof bowl, whisk egg yolks and vinegar until slightly thickened.
Place the bowl over a pot of simmering water (not boiling).
Continue whisking until the mixture becomes pale and creamy — ribbons should form when the whisk is lifted.
Slowly drizzle in warm clarified butter while whisking continuously. Add a few drops at a time at first, then in a thin steady stream.
Once thick and glossy, season with salt, cayenne, and lemon juice to taste.
Keep warm (not hot) until service — ideally at 40–45°C (104–113°F).
Chef's Tip: If the sauce splits, whisk in a teaspoon of hot water or a new egg yolk to re-emulsify.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Plating
steps: Spoon a generous pool of Hollandaise onto a pre-warmed plate.
Slice or leave the steak whole; place it elegantly over the sauce.
Add grilled asparagus or your chosen sides.
Garnish with microgreens and Maldon sea salt flakes.
Serve immediately while the steak is juicy and the Hollandaise is silky.

servingSuggestions.title: Chef's Signature Touch
items: Brush the steak with a touch of truffle oil before serving for a luxury aroma.
A sprinkle of smoked paprika or chive dust adds visual contrast and depth.
Serve with Dauphinoise potatoes or Pommes Anna for a true Continental fine-dining pairing.

chefTips: Bring steaks to room temperature before grilling for even cooking.
Do not move the steaks too early to achieve perfect grill marks.
Rest the steaks before serving to retain their juices.
Keep the Hollandaise warm, not hot, to prevent splitting.
If the Hollandaise splits, whisk in a teaspoon of hot water or a fresh egg yolk to restore the emulsion.
